text:
andrew: Heads-up — noticed a p95 spike on prod after last runtime deploy (commit dd3a9f3). Looks related to admit path and KV hit rates dropping. Graph: small burst -> lots of 429s then recovery. :thinking:

maria: which kernel change was in that deploy? was it the attention tiling fallback?

andrew: yep, we swapped kernel selector to prefer wave-kernel for long sequences (opt heuristic). Also bumped continuous-batcher window from 8->12ms. suspect batcher grew and evicted more KV entries -> lower KV hit -> longer token work.

jon: can you paste the perf traces? any tail latency stack samples?

andrew: pasted below
```
trace_id=abc123
op=serve_request
step=admit_queue wait_ms=18
step=batch_assemble size=24
step=kernel_exec time_ms=67
kv_hit=false
```

sophie: 24 is big for that workload. Our token_budget target is still 512 but per-request tokens are small; continuous batcher didn't enforce per-lane token caps.

maria: is soft-429 rate high only for that cohort (long seq), or system-wide?

andrew: concentrated on one lane (customer X) — but spillover impacted co-located lanes. soft-429s rose from 0.3%->4.8% over 10m.

jon: hypothesis: larger batches increase kernel_exec time non-linearly and cause backlog that causes the admit controller to start soft-shedding. Also KV cache size is fixed so larger batches mean fewer unique requests hit the cache (eviction).

sophie: agree. Quick mitigation: reduce continuous-batcher max-window back to 8ms and add token-budget enforcement per-lane: if batch would exceed lane_token_cap, split.

maria: can we add a temporary routing rule: route long-seq requests to wave-kernel-exclusive hosts to avoid evicting KV on small-kernel hosts?

andrew: we can, but provisioning is slow. prefer a config flip: kernel-selector fallback to preferring small-batch kernels when kv_hit_rate < 0.6. cheap to flip.

infra-bot: deploybot: started rollback of commit dd3a9f3 to canary (svc=runtime-canary)

jon: also want to capture profiling info: per-batch kernel time vs batch size for both kernels. If we have that, can model expected queueing delay and adjust admit token budget target accordingly.

sophie: I'll add a perf job to sweep batch sizes and kernel choices. Will post CSV to /mnt/builds/bench/216543-perf.csv when done.

maria: action items
- rollback kernel selector on canary (infra)
- restore batcher window to 8ms (andrew)
- add per-lane token cap check (sophie)
- collect kernel vs batch-size profile (jon)

andrew: thanks. Will monitor soft-429 rate and KV hit. If we still see >1% after changes, next step is temporary rate-limiting for the offending customer.

sophie: noted. :eyes:
